#image("/imgs/ap-calc-ab-2009-frq-04-diagram-01.png", width: 65%)

Let $R$ be the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the graphs of $y = 2 x$ and $y = x^(2)$, as shown in the figure above.

(a) Find the area of $R$.

(b) The region $R$ is the base of a solid. For this solid, at each $x$ the cross section perpendicular to the $x$-axis has area $A(x)= sin lr((frac(pi,2) x))$. Find the volume of the solid.

(c) Another solid has the same base $R$. For this solid, the cross sections perpendicular to the $y$-axis are squares. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid.
